title: A clique with a five-edge tail reverses the hubs-biased Kirchhoff ordering
exact_endpoint: KirchhoffReal.refuteSpec : ¬ LiteralConjecture GroupInverse spectralIndex (Lemma 4.6 spectral reading, primary substantive result); KirchhoffReal.refuteMP : ¬ LiteralConjecture Penrose pairIndex (literal (4.3) Moore-Penrose reading)
scope: Estrada-Mugnolo (J. Math. Anal. Appl. 507 (2022) 125728, arXiv:2101.07103) Conjecture 4.13 asserts R_1 >= R_0 >= R_-1 for hubs-biased Kirchhoff indices, with equality iff regular. The spectral index the authors computed (Lemma 4.6, n*tr of the group inverse) satisfies the ordering for all 12,103 connected graphs with 5<=n<=8 (independent review), but K6 with a pendant five-edge path has R_1 = 1696684/14035 < 370/3 = R_0. The literal Moore-Penrose reading (4.3) also fails there (515538204/7137235) and already fails at n=5, an uncredited source inconsistency.
source_targets: E. Estrada, D. Mugnolo, arXiv:2101.07103v2 Conjecture 4.13; J. Math. Anal. Appl. 507 (2022) 125728
substantive_reason: Refutes a published conjecture on hubs-biased resistance/Kirchhoff indices in the regime the authors actually tested (spectral reading holds through n=8, fails at n=11), with exact certificates and uniqueness of both inverses; one result only.
novelty_standard: Qualified bounded comparison; not worldwide priority
remaining_literature_limits: Chaos 33 (2023) biased-Kuramoto paper only partially read
trust_limits: eigenvalue-to-trace identification proved ordinarily, not in Lean (the Lean spectral endpoint is the group-inverse trace)
not_claimed: Global minimality (smallest spectral counterexample order in [9,11])
